This is a well-structured, accessible HTML5 document demonstrating modern best practices for semantic markup and inclusive design.

It uses semantic landmarks, a skip link for keyboard navigation, and CSS that adapts to your light or dark mode preference.

Text and link colors meet WCAG AA contrast in both themes, type scales with your browser's font size, and motion respects your system settings.

Features

  • Semantic HTML structure with proper landmarks
  • Keyboard accessible navigation and focus management
  • Dark mode support with custom color schemes
  • Responsive typography using modern CSS
  • Print-friendly styles for better readability
  • WCAG AA contrast compliance in all color modes

Examples

Component Cards

Card components are useful for organizing related content. They include a subtle border and padding for visual separation.

Learn more about accessibility resources

Interactive Elements

Buttons and links are fully accessible with clear focus states. All interactive elements include visible focus indicators and proper ARIA labels.

Keyboard navigation: Use Tab to move forward, Shift+Tab to move backward, and Enter or Space to activate.

Accessible Form

Fields marked * are required.

For example, name@example.com

Click the button to announce a message using a live region. This demonstrates how screen readers are notified of dynamic updates.

This counter demonstrates state management and ARIA live regions for accessible dynamic content.

content.text:
`0.html` was already in good shape, so I made six targeted fixes rather than a rewrite. None of it has been run: the syntax check I tried was blocked by the session's permissions, and I haven't opened the page in a browser.

## What changed

All of these are in `/private/tmp/cgmzd/0.html`:

| Problem | Fix |
|---|---|
| `novalidate` was hard-coded in the markup, so without JavaScript the form had no validation at all | It is now set from the script, so native browser validation still works if the script doesn't run |
| The "Sending your message…" status was shown in green success styling before anything had succeeded | The pending state now has its own neutral styling |
| Fields stayed editable while sending, so typing cleared the status and the text was then wiped by the reset | Fields are read-only while sending, and the status is no longer cleared mid-send |
| The submit button still brightened on hover and shrank on press while disabled | Hover and press effects now skip disabled buttons |
| The character counter used the browser's locale, so it could show "2.000" next to the static "2,000 characters" | The counter now formats using the page's language |
| In forced-colors (high contrast) mode the theme toggle did nothing, because system colours override the page theme | The toggle is hidden in that mode |

## Left alone

- **Placeholder URLs:** the canonical link (`https://www.example.com`) and the GitHub footer link are placeholders and need real URLs from you.
- **`dns-prefetch` hints:** the four hints point at sites that are only outbound links, so they add DNS lookups for pages most visitors won't open. I'd remove them, but that's your call.

The form flow is the part worth a quick manual check: submit with an empty email, then a valid one.
